title: Pretty Persuasion
full_review:
"Pretty Persuasion" (Samuel Goldwyn) is anything but pretty. In fact director Marcos Siega's cynical, mean-spirited and unjustifiably raunchy revenge tale makes other dark-edged teen satires like "Heathers," "Election" and "Mean Girls" look positively cheery by comparison and makes their respective bobby-socked bad girls out to be candy stripers.

The film centers on aspiring actress Kimberly Joyce (Evan Rachel Wood), a narcissistic and maliciously manipulative 15-year-old attending an exclusive private school in Beverly Hills. With the face of an angel, the tongue of a viper and the heart of Lady Macbeth, Kimberly uses her seductive charm to get what she wants.

As they say, the poisoned apple didn't fall far from tree. Her father, Hank (James Woods), is a racist slob who goes off on obscenity-laced anti-Semitic rants at the dinner table, snorts cocaine and masturbates while engaging in phone sex. (The sleazy shot of Woods fondling himself in a ratty bathrobe is perhaps the film's nadir of bad taste.)

Kimberly seems to take special relish in mercilessly tongue-lashing her stepmother (Jamie King) with depraved accusations. (Her estranged biological mother barely acknowledges her existence.)

For reasons only later revealed, she recruits two classmates -- best-friend Brittany (Elisabeth Harnois) and strictly-raised Middle Eastern transplant Randa (Adi Schnall) -- in accusing one of their high-school teachers, Percy Anderson (Ron Livingston), of sexual misconduct, entangling all involved in her grand Machiavellian web of deceit that has tragic consequences.

Despite an absence of nudity, there are numerous extremely provocative and exploitative scenes, including several of teens engaging in oral sex -- in one instance involving Kimberly and an adult lesbian TV reporter (Jane Krakowski) -- anal sex and masturbation, as well as those of Percy lustfully ogling female students.

The film also has a gratuitous amount of sordid language, much of which is either spoken by (or, equally troubling, directed at) Kimberly.

Despite a mesmerizing performance by its Lolitaish lead, "Pretty Persuasion" lacks any sympathetic characters, except Randa, and its alleged "humor" is just too distasteful to be funny.

And while having pretensions of social commentary -- on such issues as the media, racism, cultural assimilation, domestic dysfunction, adolescent angst and obsession with celebrity -- the movie seems content to shock rather than enlighten (or for that matter entertain), offering no real insights on the themes explored.

The film contains recurring sexual situations, including suggested sodomy and oral sex between minors, and, in one case, between a teenage girl and an adult woman; masturbation; a suicide; brief drug content; same-sex kissing; excessive explicit sexual language; and some profanity, ethnic slurs and lewd humor. The USCCB Office for Film & Broadcasting classification is O -- morally offensive. Not rated by the Motion Picture Association of America.
